messages:
Ava (architecture): Quick follow-up to the RFC — we need to decide where the "schema harmonizer" lives. do we ship a lightweight adapter at the edge CDN, keep it in runtime, or force SDKs to normalize?
Diego (eng-runtime): my vote is runtime. single place to handle KV cache shaping & streaming frames. easier to reason about performance.
Priya (eng-infra): runtime sounds tidy but ops burden increases (stateful transforms + rollout risk). at infra level we could front it with a transparent sidecar per-node to limit blast radius.
Sam (eng-platform): pushing to SDKs shifts complexity to customers and fragments telemetry. we need a unified metric for compatibility failures. SDK approach = more support tickets.
Nora (eng-ml): important for model safety: harmonizer must preserve instruction tokens & stop sequences exactly. doing this at edge risks subtle truncation bugs if we rewrite frames.
Diego (eng-runtime): agreed re: stop tokens. also if we do it in runtime we can reuse existing canonicalizer code and test fixtures from v2->v3 migrations.
Priya (eng-infra): ops tradeoff: runtime adapter means we need feature flags + phased rollout hooks and a canary path. sidecar lets infra own rollouts without touching runtime binary.
Sam (eng-platform): telemetry: whatever we choose must emit a single tag e.g., compat.harmonizer="edge|runtime|sdk" so product/alerting can measure regressions. can we standardize that now?
Ava (architecture): yes, add a minimal observability contract: compat.harmonizer and compat.version_mapped. keep event schema tiny.
Diego (eng-runtime): question: should harmonizer be reversible? i.e., add envelope metadata so runtime->model sees unified shape but logs original request. concerns about PII.
Nora (eng-ml): we should avoid logging full original prompts. instead record a hash + original_version_identifier. that preserves privacy while enabling rollback debugging.
Priya (eng-infra): operational plan idea: implement runtime harmonizer behind a toggle, enable for 10% tenants in staging, track error-rate and latency delta, then canary to 1 region, etc. same rollout plan as other runtime features.
Sam (eng-platform): compatibility mapping table needs to live in source control with automated tests. small DSL? example mapping:
```
- from: v1.chat.stream
  to: v2.chat.chunked_stream
  transforms:
    - rename: { field: "messages", to: "chat_history" }
    - insert: { field: "metadata.client_version", value_from: header("Client-Version") }
```
Diego (eng-runtime): +1 on mapping-as-code. runtime can validate and precompile these. also we can auto-generate shim-telemetry from it.
Ava (architecture): decision proposal: primary implementation = runtime harmonizer (feature-flagged). secondary: sidecar pattern for high-risk tenants who want infra-level control. SDK helpers for best-effort normalization only.
Priya (eng-infra): ack, but ops asks for a documented escape hatch: tenant-level opt-out via header and a circuit-breaker to bypass harmonizer for debugging.
Sam (eng-platform): will add the observability contract and a pipeline to export compat metrics.
Nora (eng-ml): I'll prepare a small test-suite of golden prompts to run during rollout to detect subtle output shifts.
Ava (architecture): thanks. next steps: Diego to draft runtime PR with mapping-as-code loader + feature flag, Priya to sketch sidecar ops runbook, Sam to wire metrics contract, Nora to supply golden prompts. we'll reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: New feature flag created: feature.compat_harmonizer (expires in 90d)
Sam (eng-platform): noted. I'll start the dashboard skeleton and a baseline run to capture current latency for comparison.
Diego (eng-runtime): drafting PR now, will link in the RFC thread and ping for review.
Ava (architecture): great — thanks everyone.
